key_insight: Source localization in turbulent flow can be framed as a backward-transport inference problem, where detections are used to sample likely emission points via a learned Schrödinger bridge.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical, Galilean-invariant search strategy for chemical sensing and olfactory tracking that can outperform classical reactive methods across changing wind conditions.
method: Learn a backward propagator for passive tracers from detections to plausible source locations.
Use Schrödinger bridge/Langevin dynamics to sample candidate emission points.
Interpret the drift as a unified transport principle linking chemotaxis and cast-and-surge.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that, in two-dimensional turbulence, the backtracking framework outperforms classical strategies across varying wind regimes using a single learned propagator.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of the learned backward transport model and its ability to generalize across flow regimes and sparse/noisy detections.
paper_title: Learning Backward Transport for Source Localization
